{"id": "827cf4b9-1378-47bf-ad4c-8254ef324f41", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_0BQLqD79uKO79BfD2EkmBP", "content": "[{'text': '## Documentation search results\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Direct Connect routing policies and BGP communities\",\"context\":\"#### Local preference BGP communities\\\\n\\\\nYou can use local preference BGP community tags to achieve load balancing and\\\\nroute preference for incoming traffic to your network. For each prefix that you\\\\nadvertise over a BGP session, you can apply a community tag to indicate the\\\\npriority of the associated path for returning traffic.\\\\n\\\\nThe following local preference BGP community tags are supported:\\\\n\\\\n* `7224:7100`\u2014Low preference\\\\n* `7224:7200`\u2014Medium preference\\\\n* `7224:7300`\u2014High preference\\\\n\\\\nLocal preference BGP community tags are mutually exclusive. To load balance\\\\ntraffic across multiple Direct Connect connections (active/active) homed to the same\\\\nor different AWS Regions, apply the same community tag; for example,\\\\n`7224:7200` (medium preference) across the prefixes for the\\\\nconnections. If one of the connections fails, traffic will be then load balance\\\\nusing ECMP across the remaining active connections regardless of their home\\\\nRegion associations . To support failover across multiple\\\\nDirect Connect connections (active/passive), apply a community tag with a higher\\\\npreference to the prefixes for the primary or active virtual interface and a\\\\nlower preference to the prefixes for the backup or passive virtual interface.\\\\nFor example, set the BGP community tags for your primary or active virtual\\\\ninterfaces to `7224:7300` (high preference) and\\\\n`7224:7100` (low preference) for your passive virtual\\\\ninterfaces.\\\\n\\\\nLocal preference BGP community tags are evaluated before any AS_PATH\\\\nattribute, and are evaluated in order from lowest to highest preference (where\\\\nhighest preference is preferred)\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/routing-and-bgp.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How do I set up an Active/Passive Direct Connect connection to AWS?\",\"context\":\"### Influencing inbound traffic to an on-premises location from AWS\\\\n\\\\nFor an **Active/Passive** configuration of Direct Connect connections:\\\\n\\\\n* Apply the [local preference BGP community tag](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/routing-and-bgp.html#bgp-communities-private-transit). Set a higher preference to the advertised prefixes for the primary or active connection. Then, set a medium or lower preference for the passive connection.\\\\n* AS Path prepend using a shorter AS path on the active connection and a longer AS path on the passive connection.\\\\n* Advertise the most specific route using BGP on the active connection.\\\\n\\\\n**Note:**\\xa0AS Path prepending can\\'t be used to configure Active/Passive connections in the following scenarios:\\\\n\\\\n* Connection A (virtual interface VIF-A) is in Region 1.\\\\n* Connection B (virtual interface VIF-B) is in Region 2.\\\\n* Both virtual interfaces connect to a VPC in Region 1 using a Direct Connect gateway.\\\\n* Both virtual interfaces advertise the same prefixes with the same BGP attributes (such as AS Path and MED) on both connections from the on-premises location.\\\\n\\\\nFor these scenarios, outbound traffic from the VPC to the on-premises location prefers Connection A due to being in the same Region as the VPC. To setup Active/Passive Direct Connect connections in this scenario, apply a [local preference BGP community tag](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/routing-and-bgp.html#bgp-communities-private-transit). Also, you can advertise a more specific route on an active connection\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/direct-connect-active-passive-connection\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"How can I use BGP communities to influence the preferred routing path on Direct Connect links from AWS to my network?\",\"context\":\"Short description\\\\n-----------------\\\\n\\\\nTo configure [private and transit virtual interfaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/routing-and-bgp.html#bgp-communities-private-transit) to prioritize the interface that AWS uses to route traffic to your network, use the AS\\\\\\\\_PATH attribute. Direct Connect also supports local preference BGP community tags to control the route preference of traffic on private and transit virtual interfaces.\\\\n\\\\n**Note:** AWS routers evaluate local preference BGP community tags before they evaluate the AS\\\\\\\\_PATH attribute.\\\\n\\\\nResolution\\\\n----------\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/direct-connect-bgp-communities\"}]}}\\n\\n## Recent AWS announcements (What\\'s New)\\n\\nNewer than your training data may be. {"id": "df5626ac-e830-44d6-8ddd-bd4ed6d7e134", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Since outbound/inbound preference work differently, here's how to steer traffic between two Direct Connect locations attached to the same Transit Gateway:

**Outbound traffic (from AWS to on-premises):** This is controlled by what your on-premises routers advertise to AWS over BGP, not by Transit Gateway config itself.

- **AS_PATH prepending** — advertise the prefix with a longer AS path at the location you want to be secondary/backup. AWS routers prefer the shorter path.
- **Local preference BGP community tags** — tag the prefixes you advertise with one of:
  - `7224:7100` — Low preference
  - `7224:7200` — Medium preference
  - `7224:7300` — High preference

  Set a higher-preference tag on the location you want preferred. AWS evaluates these **before** AS_PATH, so they take priority if you set both.
- **Advertise a more-specific prefix** from the preferred location — longest prefix match wins regardless of AS_PATH or community tags.

**Inbound traffic (from on-premises to AWS/VPC):** Controlled from your on-premises router by giving the preferred Direct Connect connection's BGP session a better local preference or shorter AS path on your side, since AWS will just honor standard BGP best-path selection on the routes it receives.

One caveat from AWS's guidance: if both virtual interfaces are in different Regions but connect to a VPC in the same Region via a Direct Connect gateway, and both advertise identical AS_PATH/MED, AS_PATH prepending alone won't work for outbound preference — you'd need the local preference BGP community tags instead to override that behavior.

If you want, I can also check your specific Direct Connect virtual interface and BGP configuration to see what's currently advertised at each location.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
